propositions: Code review lacks a dedicated concurrency correctness criterion; security and performance overlays cover only narrow subsets (TOCTOU and load-shaped races) while base reviewer has no concurrency rubric, leaving production races undetected

A two-tier deterministic lexical trigger (committed high-precision token-based + project-extensible noisy vocabulary) enables the overlay to catch both explicit synchronization primitive races and repo-modal unlocked-twin races without embedding analysis

The committed tier deliberately excludes unlocked-twin modal races (raw git rm/commit, getmtime-then-remove patterns) via design; project-specific vocabulary in criteria_routing.json supplies recall for repo-local races without baking them into the portable built-in
The overlay is registered as advisory (block_threshold 0.95, blocking_enabled false) pending calibration; strict blocking is out of scope

A project can extend built-in overlay trigger vocabulary and `applies_to` globs through `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` without code changes, enabling rebar to dogfood its own concurrency vocabulary including project tokens like `index.lock`
